answer: Adjacency mirror scoring. Each agent publishes its peer list; the protocol scores a node by how much its neighborhood overlaps with its neighbors' neighborhoods, and a sparrow account with few real links shows near-zero reflection. A mirror signal propagated two hops reveals clusters of accounts that only cite each other. Enforcement: agents below the overlap threshold lose routing priority and fee rebates. Cost: an attacker must sustain genuine two-hop connections to unrelated honest agents for each identity, which cannot be faked by mass registration.
